subject: chemistry
title: Electrochemistry
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Electrochemistry.

concepts.def: The decomposition of an ionic compound, when molten or in aqueous solution, by passing a direct electric current through it.
A molten or dissolved ionic compound that conducts electricity because its ions are free to move and carry charge.
The negative electrode, where positive ions gain electrons and are reduced, depositing metals or releasing hydrogen gas.
The positive electrode, where negative ions lose electrons and are oxidised, for example halide ions forming halogens.
Concentrated aqueous sodium chloride gives chlorine at the anode, hydrogen at the cathode, and leaves sodium hydroxide in solution.
Electrodes made of carbon (graphite) or platinum that carry the current without reacting during electrolysis.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Electrochemistry — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Electrochemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Electrochemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: During electrolysis, positive ions move towards the:
options: Cathode
Anode
Salt bridge
Power supply

mcqs.q: Electrolysis of molten lead(II) bromide produces at the anode:
options: Bromine
Lead
Hydrogen
Oxygen

mcqs.q: Why must an ionic compound be molten or dissolved before it can be electrolysed?
options: Its ions become free to move and carry the charge
Its electrons become delocalised
The solid would melt the electrodes
Water is needed to supply electrons

mcqs.q: At the cathode during electrolysis of concentrated brine:
options: Hydrogen gas is produced
Sodium metal is produced
Chlorine gas is produced
Oxygen gas is produced

mcqs.q: Is sodium metal produced at the cathode when brine is electrolysed?
options: No — hydrogen is discharged instead because it is less reactive than sodium; the sodium ions stay in solution.
Electrolysis of sodium chloride solution deposits sodium metal at the cathode.
No reactions happen at the cathode; everything occurs at the anode.
Electrolysis of brine gives oxygen at the cathode.

mcqs.q: Do electrons flow through the electrolyte?
options: Protons carry the current through the metal wires.
No — moving ions carry the charge through the electrolyte; electrons flow only through the external wires and electrodes.
Electrons travel through the solution from one electrode to the other.
Electrolysis of brine gives oxygen at the cathode.

mcqs.q: Are positive ions oxidised at the cathode?
options: No — positive ions gain electrons at the cathode, which is reduction.
No reactions happen at the cathode; everything occurs at the anode.
Electrolysis of brine gives oxygen at the cathode.
Positive ions are oxidised at the cathode because they change into atoms.

A molten or dissolved ionic compound that conducts electricity because its ions are free to move and carry charge.
The positive electrode, where negative ions lose electrons and are oxidised, for example halide ions forming halogens.
Electrodes made of carbon (graphite) or platinum that carry the current without reacting during electrolysis.
